composed-inversion-second-order: Analyze this from first principles and tell me whether it holds: "Adding a Redis read-through cache in front of our Postgres-backed product-listings API will cut p95 latency and reduce database load enough to defer the otherwise-scheduled Postgres vertical-scale upgrade for at least two quarters."
decompose-irreducibility: Analyze this claim from first principles: "A 5 MWh molten-salt thermal energy storage tank operating at 290-565 °C can round-trip electricity into heat and back with a system efficiency above 85%, making it cost-competitive with a lithium-ion battery system of the same nameplate capacity."
estimate-fermi: Reason from first principles: what is the installed capital cost of a 5 MWh molten-salt thermal energy storage system, in $/kWh of storage capacity, rebuilt from its constituent unit costs, and what does that come to per kWh delivered once amortised over its cycle life? Is it cost-competitive with lithium-ion storage?
ishikawa-fishbone: Analyze this from first principles. Northbrook Analytics is a B2B SaaS company offering a data-integration and reporting platform to mid-market operations teams. Contracts run $18,000-$40,000 per year and renew annually. In Q1 the quarterly churn rate was 4.1%; by the end of Q3 it had risen to 9.2%. Customer Success has flagged rising support-ticket volume and a drop in feature-adoption scores, but we have not identified whether churn is driven by offer gaps, pricing pressure, onboarding failure, service quality, competitive displacement, or some combination. Leadership has told us to find the root cause of churn and fix it. What is actually going on, and what should we do?
personal-general-2: Reason from first principles about this decision. We hold $60,000 in cash above an already-funded six-month emergency reserve, and carry a remaining $240,000 balance on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage at 6.25% APR with 27 years remaining. We take the standard deduction, so mortgage interest gives us no tax shield. Our marginal federal+state rate is about 28% on ordinary income and 18% on long-term capital gains and qualified dividends. Option A: put the full $60,000 toward mortgage principal. Option B: invest the full $60,000 in a broad-market index fund in a taxable brokerage account. Our horizon is 10 years. Which should we do?
personal-general: Help me think this through from first principles. I'm a software engineer, five years at my current employer in Portland, OR, in a fully remote role. A large San Francisco tech company has offered me $70K more a year (base plus equity), but it requires relocating and three days a week in the office. My partner has an established Portland-based career with no remote option. Should I take this job?
product-business-2: Analyze from first principles which of two things our B2B SaaS team should build next with one quarter of engineering capacity: the Slack integration sales prospects keep asking for, or the reporting rewrite an enterprise account has committed expansion against. Facts: over the last two quarters we logged 41 inbound Slack-integration requests across 240 active accounts (requests, not de-duplicated accounts), and no churn-survey reason code attributes a departure to the missing integration. Three of our top-ten accounts by ARR filed support tickets in the last two quarters citing reporting limitations as a renewal risk. One of them signed a letter of intent committing $180,000/year in expansion ARR contingent on the reporting rewrite shipping this quarter, with an exit clause permitting non-renewal if it does not. We have 3.2 engineer-quarters of build capacity this quarter, net of on-call and maintenance; it can fund only one of the two.
product-business: Should our B2B SaaS product add a free tier? Reason from first principles. We're at $2.4M ARR from 240 paying teams at about $10,000 per team per year. We acquire customers through outbound sales and referrals; we have no self-serve inbound channel. Finance confirms free-tier infrastructure and support costs would scale with active users, not paying users. We have never run a freemium pilot, so we don't know what our free-to-paid conversion rate would be. All our competitors have a free tier.
science-engineering-2: Analyze this failure from first principles and verify the root cause. A 1.5 MW upwind wind turbine's high-speed-shaft gearbox bearing (a generator-end cylindrical roller bearing) was removed from service after condition monitoring flagged a step increase in HSS vibration kurtosis at about 14,000 operating hours, well short of its L10 design life of ~130,000 hours. On disassembly the inner race shows axial-aligned spalling roughly 18 mm long, with crescent-shaped microcracks propagating from a subsurface origin about 0.4 mm below the raceway surface. White-etching cracks and a butterfly microstructure are visible in metallographic sections through the spall. The operator's hypothesis: the lubricant failed — viscosity too low in the cold-snap months drove boundary lubrication and the race wore through. We need the verified root cause before authorising the replacement specification.
science-engineering: Reason from first principles to size an off-grid solar system: a cabin in high-desert New Mexico at 35° N, occupied year-round by 2 adults, no grid connection. What panel array capacity (W) and battery bank capacity (kWh) do we need to meet the daily electrical load reliably? We plan to use LiFePO4 batteries and want 3 days of autonomy. Our rough load estimate is about 1.5 kWh/day.
self-application: Analyze this design decision from first principles. Our Claude Code plugin ships a single agent file that inlines the methodology body, six companion-tool procedures, the output template and the validation rubric. Two milestones after it shipped, the file measured 878 lines, against a recorded budget of ~500 lines / ~5,000 tokens enforced as a regression gate, so the budget is nominally violated by about 75%. The reflexive engineering response is to split it, extracting content into separate reference files. Before choosing any intervention: what is the budget actually optimizing for, and what should we do?
software-systems-2: Analyze this from first principles: build or buy? We're a 7-person engineering team at an early-stage B2B SaaS company (about $40K MRR, about 120 paying tenants, no enterprise customers yet), about to ship a feature that requires authenticated, per-tenant accounts. Until now the product has run behind a single shared password and a Stripe customer link. We must choose between (a) building auth in-house on an open-source library (sessions, password reset, MFA, audit log) and (b) adopting a managed identity provider such as Auth0, Clerk or WorkOS and wiring it into our service. The CTO says the choice is urgent because the gated feature is our next billed release.
software-systems: Reason from first principles about this. Our 6-year-old e-commerce platform (catalog, cart, checkout and fulfillment in a single Rails monolith of ~350 KLOC) has a CI/CD pipeline that takes about 45 minutes end-to-end. Every deploy requires a full test-suite run and a coordinated application restart, and our 12 engineers ship about 2 deploys a day. Engineering leadership has concluded: deploys are too slow, we need microservices. Are they right, and what should we do?
theoretical-limit-carnot: Reason from first principles: what is the thermal-to-electric conversion efficiency ceiling for the steam Rankine power block of a molten-salt power tower drawing heat from a 565 °C hot salt tank, and how far below that law-permitted ceiling is current practice? How much of that distance is recoverable?
